text: Year 9 teacher here. Since the ban kicked in, lunchtime is loud again. Kids playing handball instead of scrolling in a corner. Not perfect, but I'll take it.
My 15yo just showed me three ways around the age check in under a minute. All the ban did was teach kids to use VPNs and hide what they're doing from us.
Genuine question for parents: has the ban actually changed anything in your house, or did the screen time just move to group chats and games?
Mum of two. I couldn't fight Instagram on my own. Every other parent said yes, so I had to say yes. The ban finally took that pressure off all of us.
Handing my ID to a tech company so I can scroll Facebook is not 'online safety'. It's a data breach waiting to happen.
The algorithms were built to keep adults hooked. Why did we ever think 13-year-olds would handle them better?
For queer kids in country towns, online communities were the only place they felt normal. The ban cut that off and offered nothing in its place.
The ban is one tool. Without digital literacy in schools, kids will turn 16 with zero idea how any of this works.
GP in Brisbane. I've seen a lot of teenagers with anxiety and sleep problems tied to their phones. Anything that delays that by a few years is worth trying.
So my 15-year-old can't follow her netball club page, but she can still watch whatever she likes on YouTube without logging in. Make it make sense.
Every kid I coach used to show up to footy training glued to TikTok. This season they actually talk to each other before the warm-up.
The government told parents 'we've got this' and plenty switched off. Meanwhile the kids are on apps nobody's even heard of. False sense of security.
I'd love to see real data instead of anecdotes. Is anyone actually measuring whether teen mental health has improved since the ban started?
Big Tech spent millions lobbying against this. That alone tells you it was the right call.
Young people were never asked. We banned a whole generation from the public square and then wonder why they feel ignored.
Retired principal. We banned phones in class and the sky didn't fall. Same with this. Kids adapt faster than adults do.
Small business owner. Half my young customers found us on Instagram. Now I have to work out how to reach 15-year-olds who aren't allowed online.
Both sides are talking past each other. The real question is what we build for teens now, not whether the ban was good or bad.
Cyberbullying used to follow my son home every night. Now when he walks out the school gate, it stays at school. That's what this was about.
Teaching kids to swim beats fencing off the beach. They'll hit 16 and dive into the deep end with no practice at all.
